description:
**Divergence** — typed-id discipline across foundation client (jmap-base-client) vs foundation server (jmap-server) + extension-server backend traits:

Client side (jmap-base-client):
- src/request.rs:519 — `pub fn primary_account_id(&self, capability: &str) -> Option<&str>`
- src/request.rs:430, 433 — `accounts: HashMap<String, AccountInfo>`, `primary_accounts: HashMap<String, String>` (both keyed and valued as raw `String`, not `Id`)
- src/blob.rs:54, 93, 118, 165 — `pub account_id: &'a str` in 4 request parameter structs
- src/blob.rs:222, 224 — `pub account_id: Id`, `pub blob_id: Id` in `BlobUploadResponse` (INTERNAL asymmetry: request &str, response Id, within the same file)

Server side (all 8 extension-server backend traits):
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:431 — `account_id: &jmap_types::Id`
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:747 — `account_id: &jmap_types::Id`
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:611, 1018 — `account_id: &jmap_types::Id`
- All 8 extension-client `*_account_id()` accessors return `Result<&str, ClientError>` (uniformly via the foundation seam; consistent on the sibling axis but inconsistent vs the server seam)

**Caller-observable cost**: a consumer reading `BlobUploadResponse.blob_id: Id` and then wanting to download that blob has to call `.as_ref()` to convert `Id` → `&str` for the next call (within `blob.rs` alone, the request structs take `&'a str` while the response struct returns `Id`). The Session-derived `account_id: &str` value cannot be type-checked as the right account-id newtype before being substituted into URL templates.

**Maintainer cost**: workspace-policy decision is unsettled. The server-side canonical seam uses `&jmap_types::Id`; the client-side canonical seam uses raw `&str`. Within blob.rs the asymmetry is plainly avoidable. Across the workspace this is a real but defensible boundary (Session deserializes JSON strings without an "is-this-a-valid-Id" gate). Sibling-client consistency itself is clean — all 8 do the same thing. The flag is against the foundation-client policy choice, not against any sibling.

**Decision required**: should the client-side opt into typed `&Id` (with deserialize-time validation) or keep the permissive `&str` shape? The minimum cleanup, regardless of the policy direction, is the within-`blob.rs` asymmetry: request structs and response structs should agree on whether `account_id` is `&str` or `Id`.
title: jmap-base-client Session and blob request structs use raw &str for account_id / blob_id; all 8 extension-server backend traits use &jmap_types::Id — typed-id boundary inverted between client foundation and server foundation
